Definition: from G577; rejection; figuratively, loss:--casting away, loss.
BiblicalUsage: Two uses, and in both the loss is not the end. In Acts 27:22 Paul tells the terrified crew there shall be no loss of any man's life, but of the ship, and in Romans 11:15 the casting away of Israel is the reconciling of the world — and what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?
TheologicalSignificance: Loss is real in both verses, and in both it is outweighed: a ship for the lives aboard, a casting away for the reconciling of the world.
